claims.text: Security/input at the boundary (R34, P8): every case text in the rendered summary (descriptions of unreconciled lines, label, business name, refusals) is HTML-escaped; the API sends JSON with nosniff; the P8 invariant runs over 25 random statements with markup, entity, comment and token-mark pieces.

Failure modes (gap found and fixed): with CMA_RULESET set to an unknown ruleset, case_summary raised RulesetError uncaught and the server closed the connection with no response (probe: 'client error RemoteDisconnected Remote end closed connection without response'). RulesetError is now a refusal with no figures shown, tested.

claims.text: Failure modes: any failure no refusal foresees while computing the summary for / or /api/case is answered 500 'The case could not be shown.' naming nothing the case holds, instead of an unanswered connection; tested with an exception whose message is a description.

Idempotency: the summary is a read-only pure recomputation from the case files per request; it writes nothing, so repeated requests are idempotent. Reconciliation failure (R3) shows no figures for any account and reports the difference in pence and the lines; contracts tests cover single-account, debit-as-trading and multi-account cases.

claims.text: Observability: not applicable for T19 by design (no remote alerting; nothing logged, request log off so the token never reaches a log). The refusal states are visible in the API's state field (shown/empty/refused/not_reconciled) and tested.

Operability/rollback: the change is additive behind the `cma review` command, which runs only when invoked; rollback is reinstalling the previous wheel, with no data to repair. No new dependency, config or secret.

notes: Gaps for the owner (not built, they need design or belong to other tasks): (1) R52: the summary takes 2.67s at 10,000 lines here, over the 2s target, and both / and /api/case recompute the whole case per request (the page plus its script can compute it twice); caching by snapshot belongs with T22. (2) R3 across accounts: overrides.case_figures raises at the first account that does not reconcile, so when two accounts both fail, only the first account's difference and lines are reported; nothing is shown either way, but naming every account's lines needs case_figures to continue past the first failure. (3) The not-reconciled view lists every line involved with no paging; a categoriser bug leaving thousands of credits unbucketed would make one long table. (4) metrics.compute's plain ValueError on a malformed proposed repayment or VAT stagger now reaches the generic 500 rather than a named refusal; store validates both on write, so only a hand-edited case.yaml reaches it.
